title: What if Earth had rings like Saturn? 🪐
subject: planet
description:
Would you want a ring in your sky? 👇

What would happen if Earth had rings like Saturn? A ring would circle above the equator and could shade parts of the planet. Scientists at Monash University think Earth may really have had one 466 million years ago, after a passing asteroid broke apart. It is a hypothesis, not a confirmed fact, and other researchers say more evidence is needed.

Sources: Monash University ("Earth may have had a ring system 466 million years ago", 2024), Tomkins et al., Earth and Planetary Science Letters (2024), Space.com

scenes.text: You'd see a giant ring arching across the sky.
If Earth had rings like Saturn, they'd circle above the equator.
Their shadow could block sunlight and cool parts of the planet.
But here's the strange part. Earth may really have had one, 466 million years ago.
A passing asteroid broke apart into a ring. 21 craters from that time all sit near the old equator.
As the ring slowly fell, it may have helped push Earth into an ice age.
